b: Infective stage = the cyst (quadrinucleate, 10-15 micrometres), swallowed in faecally contaminated food or water (also sexual and oral-anal contact).
The cyst survives gastric acid; in the small intestine it excysts into eight small trophozoites .
Trophozoites live and multiply in the large intestine lumen (commensal, feeding on bacteria).
As the stool dries they round up into cysts (the diagnostic and transmitting stage in formed stool).
In some patients trophozoites invade the colonic wall , cause ulcers and may enter the portal blood to reach the liver .

qs.q: A hemimetabolous life cycle has which stage?
qs.e: Hemimetabolous insects undergo incomplete metamorphosis, featuring an egg, nymph, and adult stage.

qs.q: An organism without a known sexual stage in its life cycle would be classified in which of the following fungal groups?
qs.e: Fungi with no known teleomorph (sexual stage) are historically classified as Fungi Imperfecti, also known as Deuteromycetes or Mitosporic fungi. The other options represent fungal phyla with known sexual reproduction.
qs.s: Weekly Year 3: Medical Mycology Exam - August 14, 2026 (Section A: MCQs)

qs.q: Which one of the following vectors utilizes one host in its life cycle and pathogen transmission?
qs.e: Boophilus ticks are one-host ticks that complete their entire life cycle (larva, nymph, adult) on a single host animal. The other genera are either two-host or three-host ticks that drop off between life stages to molt before finding new hosts.

qs.q: Mosquito life cycle has larval instars.
qs.e: Mosquitoes undergo complete metamorphosis with four larval instars (developmental stages between molts): L1, L2, L3, and L4. After the fourth instar, the larva molts into a pupa, which then emerges as an adult mosquito. Each larval instar is progressively larger, with the fourth instar being the largest before pupation.

es.q: Outline the life cycle of a three-host tick.
es.m:
- Eggs hatch into six-legged larvae in the environment.
- Larvae feed on a first host, become engorged, detach and molt into nymphs.
- Nymphs feed on a second host, detach and molt into adults.
- Adults feed and mate on a third host; the engorged female detaches and lays eggs.
- The three hosts need not necessarily be different species; the defining feature is that each active stage feeds on a separate host.
